title: How To Teach Easy Lessons That Students Love
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin reframes three common teacher complaints — having to entertain students, lacking planning time, and competing with screens — by arguing the actual solution to all three is the same thing: deep content expertise, not entertainment or heavy preparation. His central claim is that trying to out-entertain students' phones and games is a losing strategy that only highlights how comparatively boring a classroom can seem; the real goal should be to be genuinely interesting, which requires knowing your subject matter deeply rather than planning elaborate activities. He argues that capturing student interest takes almost no preparation time once a teacher has real expert knowledge to draw from — the missing ingredient in most struggling classrooms isn't time, it's content depth. On competition with screens, he reframes it as an advantage rather than a disadvantage: a live, breathing subject-matter expert can go into idiosyncratic, specific details that no algorithm-fed feed can replicate. The concrete takeaway distilled at the end is disarmingly simple — teach something genuinely cool your students don't already know.

Because you have something they can’t get anywhere else. You are a living and breathing expert in your content area.
